name: Fall-line rhythm
summary: A compact descent that changes beat without wandering far across the mountain.
feel: Read the next pair, release thrust, flick through the combination, then settle back into a rhythm.
risk: Most demanding on a phone. Tight combinations need a slower entry and angled gate detection.
phases: Four regular turns establish the beat
Two closed gates: a quick hairpin combination
Three close, aligned gates: a flush
A held turn shifts the line across the slope
Four clean turns open toward the jump

name: Strata traverse
summary: An asymmetric sweep along an exposed layer, a compact turning pocket, then a broad descent into the basin.
feel: Commit to a long carve, skim the strata, tighten up briefly, then let the rover run toward the basin.
risk: The long traverse must remain visibly downhill. Terrain needs shaping so the rover does not stall against a ridge.
phases: Three welcoming turns on the upper shoulder
A delayed turn holds the line across the layers
Two closed gates tighten the terrace exit
A broad reverse sweep reveals the basin
Three regular turns align the launch approach

name: Crater sprint
summary: Three short turning sectors separated by breathing room. The path steps between shallow gullies instead of making one continuous S.
feel: A burst of precise turns, a clear run to reset, another burst, then a fast and readable release into the jump.
risk: Recovery stretches must not build more speed than the next sector can absorb. Entry gates should announce the slowdown.
phases: Five evenly spaced turns teach the first sector
A long linking turn moves into the next gully
A three-gate flush punctuates the second sector
A diagonal recovery leads to the final turning pocket
Four progressively easier gates release into the jump
